sample.blurb: 18 pusher strokes aimed at the inspection position, with the line camera's tracks. Parts keep stopping off-position.

# Tether calibration for 'Pusher log: parts missing the inspection window' (Factory inspection, 18 runs, 2026-10-10)
# NVIDIA Newton: XPBD averages the two materials' mu, so set both to the measured pair value.
import newton

MU_EFF = 0.5586  # part-rail sliding friction, 90% interval 0.5473 - 0.5710 (bootstrap)
object_cfg = newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=MU_EFF)
surface_cfg = newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=MU_EFF)
# builder.add_shape_box(body, hx=..., hy=..., hz=..., cfg=object_cfg)   # the part
# builder.add_ground_plane(cfg=surface_cfg)                             # the rail

ACTUATOR_GAIN = 0.9169  # pusher pressure: actual speed / commanded (0.9076 - 0.9310); scale commanded velocities

# Measured oily section along the travel axis (+y from the launch point).
FRICTION_REGION = {'y_start_m': 0.2905, 'mu_eff': 0.3190}  # y 0.281-0.300, mu 0.315-0.324
# Two surface bodies leave a seam that trips sliding objects; Tether instead switches the object's own mu
# when it crosses y_start with a Warp kernel and ground mu 0 (see sim/newton_push.py: _patch_setup).

# Perception (inspection position distance as the inspection camera reports it):
CAMERA = {'dx_m': -0.0005, 'pitch_error_deg': -1.244, 'lens_k_per_m': -0.00850}
# perceived = true * (1 + tan(pitch)) + dx + lens_k * true**2
exports.isaaclab:
"""Tether calibrated domain randomization for 'Pusher log: parts missing the inspection window' (2026-10-10).
Ranges are 90% bootstrap intervals of the measured values, not hand-picked bounds: train on what the real
table can plausibly be, nothing wider. PhysX "average" friction combine (the default) matches the measurement."""
from isaaclab.envs import mdp
from isaaclab.managers import EventTermCfg as EventTerm
from isaaclab.managers import SceneEntityCfg
from isaaclab.utils import configclass


@configclass
class CalibratedEventCfg:
    # sliding friction of the part-rail pair; static friction is not observed by a sliding test
    object_material = EventTerm(
        func=mdp.randomize_rigid_body_material,
        mode="startup",
        params={
            "asset_cfg": SceneEntityCfg("object"),
            "static_friction_range": (0.5473, 0.5710),
            "dynamic_friction_range": (0.5473, 0.5710),
            "restitution_range": (0.0, 0.0),
            "num_buckets": 64,
            "make_consistent": True,
        },
    )


# Pusher pressure: the real launch speed is 0.917x the command (90% 0.908-0.931). It belongs
# in the push action's scale (joint names: your robot's).
ACTUATOR_GAIN = 0.9169
push_action = mdp.JointVelocityActionCfg(asset_name="robot", joint_names=[".*"], scale=ACTUATOR_GAIN)


# Oily section: from y = 0.290 m (90% 0.281-0.300) the pair slides at mu 0.319
# (90% 0.315-0.324). A static rail prim whose top is flush with the first;
# shorten the first one so it ends at REGION_Y0 (overlapping coplanar surfaces leave PhysX two materials to pick from).
# Its combine mode 'min' outranks PhysX's default 'average', so the pair takes the region's value.
import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils
from isaaclab.assets import AssetBaseCfg

REGION_Y0 = 0.2905  # m along the push axis from the launch point
SURFACE_TOP_Z = 0.0  # set to your table top height
calibrated_region = AssetBaseCfg(
    prim_path="{ENV_REGEX_NS}/CalibratedRegion",
    spawn=sim_utils.CuboidCfg(
        size=(0.4, 2.0, 0.002),  # across the path, along it from REGION_Y0, thin
        collision_props=sim_utils.CollisionPropertiesCfg(),
        physics_material=sim_utils.RigidBodyMaterialCfg(static_friction=0.3190, dynamic_friction=0.3190,
                                                        friction_combine_mode="min"),
    ),
    init_state=AssetBaseCfg.InitialStateCfg(pos=(0.0, REGION_Y0 + 1.0, SURFACE_TOP_Z - 0.001)),
)
exports.markdown:
# Sim2Real calibration: Pusher log: parts missing the inspection window

Domain: **Factory inspection**. A pneumatic pusher slides a part along a rail to the inspection camera. Oil on the rail, a weaker pusher or a shifted camera puts the part off-position for inspection.

18 runs (log), structure chosen by Nemotron agent (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b). Stop residual 0 cm rms.

## What differs from your simulator

| Parameter | Sim | Real (measured) | 90% interval | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Part-rail friction | 0.800 | 0.559 | 0.547 – 0.571 | changed |
| Pusher strength (actual / commanded speed) | 1.000x | 0.917x | 0.908x – 0.931x | changed |
| Oily section starts at | none | 0.290 m | 0.281 m – 0.300 m | changed |
| Friction in the oily section | none | 0.319 | 0.315 – 0.324 | changed |
| Inspection camera offset | 0.000 m | -0.001 m | -0.008 m – 0.010 m | within noise |
| Inspection camera tilt error | 0.000 deg | -1.244 deg | -5.000 deg – 1.485 deg | within noise |
| Lens distortion | 0.000 1/m | -0.009 1/m | -0.072 1/m – 0.073 1/m | within noise |

## Predicted effect (model rollouts, not measured)

Success = stopping within 3 cm of the inspection position, over targets 0.2 m–0.6 m, for a policy trained in each simulator:

- current sim: **0%** (90%: 0–2%)
- calibrated sim: **100%** (90%: 100–100%)

## Next experiment

- run so the part stops near **0.62 m** (command 2.50): models disagree by ±1.0 cm here
- run so the part stops near **0.52 m** (command 2.35): models disagree by ±0.9 cm here
- run so the part stops near **0.43 m** (command 2.19): models disagree by ±0.9 cm here

## Agent's explanation

> Fitted model adds a low-friction patch beyond 0.29 m, adjusts actuator gain to 0.92, and corrects perception with small offset, pitch, and barrel distortion, yielding stop residuals <4 mm.

Generated by Tether Studio (NVIDIA Newton physics, Nemotron agent). Intervals: bootstrap over runs.
